text:
jen: quick note from canary: observed stale reads after a prefix handoff. repro sketch below.

jen: repro:
1) node-old owns prefix p (epoch=7)
2) node-old starts handoff -> node-new (token opaque)
3) node-new acked ownership but apply of demote/tombstone delayed (GC + CPU)
4) router sends reads to node-new; node-new served older snapshot -> stale

omar: summary: router sees ownership before receiver finished applying tombstones. we need a visible applied marker.

lina: options: 1) router waits synchronously (bad perf), 2) receiver exposes applied_epoch durable marker, router falls back while unknown, 3) make applies faster (hard). I prefer 2.

jen: propose small API change: `POST /prefix/:p/apply {epoch, nonce, tombstone_meta}` -> `{applied_epoch, already_applied}`. apply persists small manifest (prefix->last_applied_epoch) with fsync so restarts are safe.

omar: add nonce for idempotency. server logic: check nonce, check epoch > last_applied, append+fsync, update last_applied, return. keep seen-nonce window small.

lina: router behavior: on ownership change, async fetch receiver.applied_epoch (cached). if applied_epoch < epoch or missing, route to fallback (old owner or proxy) and tag with header to trigger client retry. once applied_epoch >= epoch router switches traffic.

ops-bot: deploy-note: feature-flag `applied_epoch_marker`, metrics to add: `apply.latency_ms`, `apply.nonce_conflicts`, rollout: canary -> staged -> prod.

jen: test plan: unit idempotency tests, integration with receiver crash during fsync, chaos test with churn. small benchmark for fsync cost.

omar: long-term we can piggyback applied_epoch on heartbeats to avoid extra fetches.

lina: I'll draft RFC + small prototype. sync Friday to sign off. :thumbsup:
